scripts.topic: [Pillar: SBA loans explained] Myth vs. reality: 'The SBA guarantee protects me if my business fails.' The guaranty protects the lender, the borrower still owes the full debt, and owners of 20% or more generally sign a personal guaranty.
scripts.audience: First-time SBA borrowers (franchise buyers, acquisition buyers, growth owners) who read 'government-backed' as lower personal risk
scripts.problem: Viewers misread 'government-guaranteed' as protection for the borrower, and that changes how they weigh personal risk before they borrow.
scripts.amount_context: No deal size or loan amount used. The provisional ~USD 300,000 figure is not mentioned. The only figure is the twenty percent ownership threshold for personal guaranties (as of Oct 2026, subject to change).
scripts.hook: The SBA guarantee isn't there to protect you. Here's who it protects.
scripts.script: The SBA guarantee isn't there to protect you. Here's who it protects. The myth: it's government-backed, so if my business fails, I'm covered. The reality: on an SBA seven-A loan, one of the SBA's loan programs, the SBA guarantees part of the loan to the lender. If the borrower defaults, the lender can ask the SBA to buy that guaranteed portion. You still owe the full debt. Now the twist. Owners of twenty percent or more generally must sign a full, unlimited personal guarantee. That means you're personally responsible for repaying if the business can't. And after a default, the SBA may use legal means to recover what's still owed. That's as of October twenty twenty-six, and subject to change. None of this means don't borrow. It means borrow with clear eyes. Share this with your business partner before you both sign.
scripts.cta: Share this with your business partner before you both sign.
scripts.recording_notes_es: Plano medio, mirando directo a cámara, tono sereno y sin dramatismo. Pausa breve después de 'Here's who it protects' para generar curiosidad. Cambia de postura o da un paso leve al decir 'Now the twist'. Habla más despacio en la parte del personal guarantee. Termina con una sonrisa tranquila, que no se vea como advertencia alarmista.
scripts.adaptation_note_es: De V17 solo se toma el mecanismo de 'fijar expectativas realistas' sobre los préstamos SBA. No se copian frases, guion ni historia del creador. El enfoque mito/realidad sobre a quién protege la garantía es original.

fact_refs.claim: The SBA guarantees part of a 7(a) loan to the lender; on default the lender can ask the SBA to buy the guaranteed portion; the borrower still owes the full debt.
Owners of 20% or more generally must give a full, unlimited personal guaranty (as of Oct 2026, subject to change).
After a default the remaining debt is still owed and the SBA may use all legal means available to recover it.

scripts.why_selected_es: Corrige una idea equivocada muy común con un giro claro (el personal guarantee). Es fácil de compartir entre socios o compradores antes de firmar, y no repite el mito de 'la SBA presta el dinero' de ayer.
scripts.what_to_measure_es: Compartidos y envíos por DM a terceros como métrica principal. Después, retención hasta el giro (~20 s) y guardados. Las vistas no cuentan como leads.
qa_issues: Sin problemas que impidan grabar. La parte de la garantía se apoya en fragmentos del eCFR y el 20% en fuentes de la industria. Hay que verificarlos de nuevo en SBA.gov antes de publicar.

scripts.topic: [Pillar: SBA loans explained] Inside the SBA 504 structure: bank first lien, CDC second lien funded by an SBA-guaranteed debenture, and borrower equity, plus who a CDC is.
scripts.audience: Established owners planning to buy owner-occupied real estate or major equipment; acquisition buyers whose deal includes real estate
scripts.problem: People hear '504' without knowing it means two lenders plus their own equity, so term sheets are confusing and they don't know who to talk to first.
scripts.amount_context: No dollar amount used. Percentages only (fifty / forty / ten, fifteen and twenty percent borrower contribution), as of Oct 2026, subject to change. The provisional ~USD 300,000 figure is not mentioned.
scripts.hook: An SBA five-oh-four loan is really three pieces of money stacked together.
scripts.script: An SBA five-oh-four loan is really three pieces of money stacked together. Layer one: a third-party lender, usually a bank, typically finances fifty percent of the project and holds the first lien, meaning first claim on the asset. Layer two: up to forty percent comes from a CDC, with a second lien. It's funded by a debenture, a type of bond, that the SBA guarantees one hundred percent. Layer three is you. At least ten percent equity, typically. It goes up to fifteen percent if the business has less than two years of history or the property is special-purpose, built for one specific use, and twenty percent if both apply. So who is the CDC? A Certified Development Company: a nonprofit the SBA certifies and regulates to deliver five-oh-four loans. As of October twenty twenty-six, subject to change. Confirm with your lender. Save this for your next property conversation.
scripts.cta: Save this for your next property conversation.
scripts.recording_notes_es: Plano medio, energía tranquila de explicador. Usa las manos para 'apilar' tres capas a distintas alturas (una por capa) y vuelve a ese gesto en cada 'Layer'. Pausa breve antes de 'So who is the CDC?' y baja el ritmo para la definición. Mira a cámara todo el tiempo.
scripts.adaptation_note_es: De V28 solo se toma la idea de explicar el programa 504 aplicado a la compra de inmuebles. No se copia el nicho (wedding venues), las frases ni la cifra de 'up to $5 million', que no está verificada en SBA.gov y se deja fuera.

fact_refs.claim: In a 504 loan, a third-party lender (usually a bank) holds a first lien, a CDC holds a second lien funded by a debenture the SBA guarantees 100%, and the borrower contributes equity.
Typical split 50% lender, up to 40% CDC, at least 10% borrower; 15% if under two years of operating history or special-purpose property; 20% if both (as of Oct 2026, subject to change).
A CDC is a nonprofit certified and regulated by the SBA to deliver 504 loans.

scripts.why_selected_es: Es una explicación de referencia (las tres capas y los porcentajes) que el público quiere guardar para cuando analice un inmueble. Profundiza en la estructura sin repetir la comparación 7(a) vs 504 de ayer.
scripts.what_to_measure_es: Guardados como métrica principal. Después, retención hasta la definición de CDC y DMs calificados de dueños con proyectos inmobiliarios. Las vistas no son leads.
qa_issues: Riesgo de duración: 149 palabras dan unos 61,7 s a 145 ppm. Recortar unas 5 palabras (por ejemplo, 'Confirm with your lender.' podría ir solo en el caption) o grabar a unas 150 ppm.
Detalle: la fuente dice 'at least fifty percent' para el banco. 'Typically' se acepta, pero hay que verificar de nuevo el reparto 50/40/10 y el 15%/20%.

scripts.topic: [Pillar: SBA loans explained] SBA Express vs. standard 7(a): what 'Express' changes (lender's delegated decision, smaller maximum, lower guaranty share) and what it does not mean (fast approval).
scripts.audience: Owners looking for smaller growth or working-capital loans who have seen 'SBA Express' advertised
scripts.problem: The program name suggests guaranteed speed, so owners may choose a product by its name instead of by loan size and fit.
scripts.amount_context: Program maximums only: five hundred thousand dollars (SBA Express) and five million dollars (standard 7(a)), plus the one hundred fifty thousand dollar guaranty threshold, as of Oct 2026, subject to change. The provisional ~USD 300,000 figure is not mentioned.
scripts.hook: Express doesn't mean what most people think.
scripts.script: Express doesn't mean what most people think. It's not a promise of fast approval. SBA Express is a version of the seven-A loan program, and here's what changes. First, who decides. Express lenders have delegated authority, so they make the credit decision using their own procedures, then send the guarantee request to the SBA. Second, size. As of October twenty twenty-six, Express goes up to five hundred thousand dollars. Standard seven-A goes up to five million dollars. Third, the guarantee. Express carries a fifty percent guarantee to the lender. Standard seven-A is up to eighty-five percent for loans of one hundred fifty thousand dollars or less, and seventy-five percent above that. What stays the same? A lender still has to approve your loan, and nothing about the name guarantees speed. These figures can change, so confirm with your lender. Share this with someone comparing SBA options.
scripts.cta: Share this with someone comparing SBA options.
scripts.recording_notes_es: Plano medio, tono seguro y algo pícaro en el hook, sin exagerar. Marca con los dedos 'First, Second, Third'. Pausa clara antes de 'What stays the same?' y mira fijo a cámara en 'nothing about the name guarantees speed'. Ritmo constante, sin apurarse en las cifras.
scripts.adaptation_note_es: Guion original. No se basa en ninguna referencia de creador; la comparación Express vs 7(a) estándar se construyó solo con datos verificados.

fact_refs.claim: SBA Express lenders have delegated authority, decide on credit using their own procedures and submit the guaranty request to the SBA.
SBA Express maximum is $500,000 (as of Oct 2026, subject to change).
Standard 7(a) maximum is $5 million (as of Oct 2026, subject to change).
SBA Express guaranty is 50%; standard 7(a) is up to 85% for loans of $150,000 or less and 75% above (as of Oct 2026, subject to change).

scripts.why_selected_es: El término 'SBA Express' se busca y se publicita mucho; aclarar qué significa realmente atrae a nuevos públicos (descubrimiento) y refuerza la confianza al evitar promesas de rapidez. No se cubrió ayer.
scripts.what_to_measure_es: Alcance a no seguidores, visitas al perfil y nuevos seguidores como señales de descubrimiento. Después, compartidos y retención hasta 'What stays the same?'. Las vistas no son leads.
qa_issues: No es grave: no se explica qué es el 7(a). Agregar 'the SBA's main loan program' después de 'the seven-A loan program'.
Verificar de nuevo el 50%, el 85%/75% y los máximos de USD 500.000 y USD 5 millones.

scripts.topic: [Pillar: SBA loans explained] 'What happens after I apply for an SBA loan?' Stage map: underwriting, SBA guaranty step (delegated or not), closing requirements, closing and funding. No timelines.
scripts.audience: Borrowers about to apply or who have just applied (franchise buyers, acquisition buyers, growth owners)
scripts.problem: Not knowing what comes after submission creates anxiety and missed requests; borrowers don't expect closing requirements such as a business valuation.
scripts.amount_context: No dollar amount used. The provisional ~USD 300,000 figure is not mentioned.
scripts.hook: You hit submit on your SBA loan application. Then what?
scripts.script: You hit submit on your SBA loan application. Then what? Here's the general path, and it varies by lender and deal. Stage one: underwriting. The lender reviews your application and decides on the loan. Stage two: the SBA step. Some lenders have delegated authority, meaning they approve the loan themselves and submit it electronically for an SBA loan number. Other lenders send it to an SBA processing center, which reviews it and issues the loan number if approved. Stage three is where surprises show up: closing requirements. As of October twenty twenty-six, subject to change, buying a business generally requires an independent business valuation. If an agent is paid, there's a fee disclosure form. Insurance and lien filings, the lender's recorded claim on assets, are common. Stage four: closing and funding. No stage comes with a guaranteed timeline. Which stage feels least clear? Tell us in a DM.
scripts.cta: Which stage feels least clear? Tell us in a DM.
scripts.recording_notes_es: Plano medio, tono empático, como quien acompaña a alguien ansioso. En el hook, gesto breve de 'enviar' con la mano y pausa en 'Then what?'. Marca cada etapa con los dedos. Baja un poco la voz y acércate a cámara en 'Stage three is where surprises show up' para sostener la atención. Cierra con una pregunta genuina, mirando a cámara.
scripts.adaptation_note_es: De V17 solo se toma el mecanismo de fijar expectativas ('el proceso puede ser exhaustivo'). Se adapta como mapa de etapas posterior a la solicitud; no se copian frases ni contenido del creador.

fact_refs.claim: The lender underwrites; delegated lenders approve and submit via E-Tran where the SBA assigns a loan number; for other lenders the SBA's processing center reviews and issues the loan number if approved.
Under SOP 50 10 8.1 (effective for loan numbers on or after Oct 1, 2026), change-of-ownership deals require an independent business valuation (as of Oct 2026, subject to change).
If an agent is paid in connection with the loan, SBA Form 159 (Fee Disclosure and Compensation Agreement) is required.
Insurance and lien filings are commonly part of closing; varies by lender and deal.

scripts.why_selected_es: El formato de etapas con un bucle abierto ('stage three is where surprises show up') mantiene la atención hasta el final y reduce la ansiedad de quien ya aplicó. Va más allá de lo cubierto ayer (objeción del papeleo y elección de prestamista). Se omitió la commitment letter por no estar verificada.
scripts.what_to_measure_es: Retención promedio y porcentaje que llega a la etapa cuatro como métrica principal. Después, DMs con preguntas sobre una etapa concreta (calificados) y guardados. Las vistas no son leads.
qa_issues: La valuación obligatoria bajo 8.1 solo tiene respaldo de una fuente de la industria. El guion la matiza con 'generally' y 'subject to change', pero hay que verificarla de nuevo antes de publicar.
Riesgo de duración: 148 palabras dan unos 61 s a 145 ppm. Recortar un poco.

scripts.topic: [SBA loans explained] Objection: 'I don't have enough collateral, so I can't get an SBA loan.' How SBA collateral rules work by loan size, as of October 2026
scripts.audience: Owners and buyers without much hard collateral (service businesses, first-time buyers) who rule themselves out of SBA loans
scripts.problem: People assume they can't qualify because of collateral, so they never have the conversation. Others don't realize their personal home equity may come into play on larger loans.
scripts.amount_context: SBA program thresholds only (as of Oct 2026, subject to change): $50,000; $350,000; $500,000 for SBA Express. These are not deal-size figures and the provisional ~$300,000 is not used.
scripts.hook: "I don't have enough collateral, so I can't get an SBA loan." Here's what the rules say.
scripts.script: "I don't have enough collateral, so I can't get an SBA loan." Here's what the rules say. As of October twenty twenty-six, and subject to change: for seven-A loans of fifty thousand dollars or less, the SBA doesn't require collateral. Between that and three hundred fifty thousand, lenders follow their own collateral policy for similar loans. For SBA Express, that lender-policy range goes up to five hundred thousand. Above those amounts, lenders must take available collateral to the maximum extent possible. And here's the key part: an otherwise eligible loan isn't supposed to be declined only because collateral falls short. But that's not a yes. The lender still decides, so confirm with yours. And on larger loans, if business assets don't cover it, lenders may need to look at equity in your personal real estate. Not sure how your collateral picture fits? Send us a DM.
scripts.cta: Not sure how your collateral picture fits? Send us a DM.
scripts.recording_notes_es: Plano medio, mirando a cámara. Dice la objeción con tono de cliente, algo escéptico, y luego hace una pausa de un segundo antes de 'Here's what the rules say'. Al dar los tramos, marca con la mano tres niveles (bajo, medio, alto). Baja el ritmo y pone voz seria en 'But that's not a yes'. Cierre cálido y sin prisa.
scripts.adaptation_note_es: Original. No se adapta ningún video de referencia. Se usa el mecanismo genérico de objeción y luego un 'sí, pero' en dos partes.

fact_refs.claim: As of Oct 2026: no collateral required for 7(a) loans of $50,000 or less; from $50,001 to $350,000 lenders follow their own policy for similar non-SBA loans; above that, lenders must take available collateral to the maximum extent possible
SBA Express lenders may apply their own collateral policy for loans over $50,000 up to $500,000
An otherwise-eligible loan is not to be declined solely because collateral is inadequate (paraphrased, not quoted)

If business assets don't fully secure a larger loan, lenders must take available equity in owners' personal real estate (phrased with 'may', 25% threshold omitted; confirm under SOP 50 10 8.1 before airing)

scripts.why_selected_es: Nadie lo cubrió ayer. Es una objeción que hace que buena gente se autodescarte, y responderla con la regla real abre conversaciones calificadas sin prometer aprobación.
scripts.what_to_measure_es: DMs calificados que mencionen garantías o colateral, retención hasta el 'But that's not a yes', guardados y visitas al perfil. Las vistas no cuentan como leads.
qa_issues: La frase 'on larger loans, if business assets don't cover it, lenders may need to look at equity in your personal real estate' viene de un snippet de fuente mixta. La investigación pide expresamente 'Confirm under 8.1 before using', y el propio fact_ref dice 'confirm before airing'. Arreglo: confirmarla en la SOP 50 10 8.1 antes de grabar o quitar la frase.

Los tramos de colateral (cincuenta mil, trescientos cincuenta mil y quinientos mil para Express) salen de resúmenes de la industria sobre la SOP 50 10 8, con la nota 'confirm in 8.1'. Sin embargo, el guion los fecha 'As of October twenty twenty-six', cuando ya rige la 8.1. Arreglo: confirmarlos en la 8.1 o reformular como 'Under the SBA's SOP 50 10 8 rules, and subject to change, ...', sin atribuirlos a octubre de 2026.
No bloqueante: 'Here's what the rules say' anticipa una cita textual. Como la regla de no rechazar solo por falta de colateral está parafraseada, conviene 'Here's how the rules work'.

scripts.topic: [Buying a franchise] Hypothetical scenario: royalties and the ad fund come off monthly sales before rent, payroll and the loan payment
scripts.audience: Prospective franchisees comparing brands who focus on revenue claims
scripts.problem: Buyers judge a franchise by gross sales and underestimate ongoing fees calculated on revenue, which shrinks the cash left for debt service.
scripts.amount_context: Hypothetical: $50,000 in monthly gross sales, a hypothetical 6% royalty ($3,000) and a hypothetical 2% ad fund ($1,000). Not real brand data and not the provisional deal-size figure.
scripts.hook: Your franchise does fifty thousand dollars in sales this month. Here's what comes off the top before anything else gets paid.
scripts.script: Your franchise does fifty thousand dollars in sales this month. Here's what comes off the top before anything else gets paid. This is a hypothetical, with round numbers. Say the royalty, your ongoing fee to the franchisor, is six percent of gross sales. That's three thousand dollars gone. Say the ad fund is two percent. Another thousand. Now you're at forty-six thousand, and you haven't paid rent, payroll, supplies or utilities yet. And then the loan payment. That comes out of whatever's left after all of that. The Federal Trade Commission's franchise guide notes royalties may be based on a percentage of your gross income, even in a month you lose money. Your real fees, and how each one is calculated, are listed in Item six of the franchise disclosure document. Save this, and run your own numbers before you compare brands.
scripts.cta: Save this, and run your own numbers before you compare brands.
scripts.recording_notes_es: Plano medio con energía tranquila. En cada resta, pausa breve, como si contara con los dedos. Pausa marcada antes de 'And then the loan payment' para crear expectativa. Mirada directa y tono serio en la parte de la FTC. Sonrisa leve en el cierre.
scripts.adaptation_note_es: De V21 solo se toma el mecanismo de explicar la jerga de las regalías. No se copia texto ni historia. Se suma una 'cascada' hipotética propia y la referencia oficial a Item 6.

fact_refs.claim: FDD Item 6 discloses other recurring or occasional fees paid to the franchisor, such as royalties and advertising fees
The FTC guide says royalties may be based on a percentage of weekly or monthly gross income, even if you are losing money (paraphrased)
$50,000 sales, 6% royalty, 2% ad fund and the resulting $46,000 are hypothetical round numbers

scripts.why_selected_es: Es un tema de flujo de caja continuo (Item 6) que no cubrimos ayer (Item 7/9). La cascada numérica retiene y da ganas de guardar el video para hacer las propias cuentas.
scripts.what_to_measure_es: Guardados, retención hasta el 'And then the loan payment', compartidos y DMs sobre franquicias. Las vistas no son leads.
qa_issues: No bloqueante: 'Your real fees, and how each one is calculated, are listed in Item six' exagera, porque la cuota inicial de franquicia está en el Item 5. Arreglo: 'Your ongoing fees, and how each one is calculated, are listed in Item six'.

No bloqueante: 'before anything else gets paid' sugiere un orden de pago real. Se puede suavizar con 'Here's what comes off the top, on paper, before anything else'. El dos por ciento del fondo de publicidad ya está marcado como hipotético, así que no contradice la guía de la investigación.

scripts.topic: [Buying a franchise] Resale franchise vs. new unit: operating history vs. projections, transfer terms and fee, valuation on a change of ownership, Franchise Directory
scripts.audience: Prospective franchisees deciding between a resale and a new unit within the next year
scripts.problem: Buyers don't realize a resale is a transfer and a change of ownership with its own steps, while a new unit relies only on projections.
scripts.amount_context: No amounts used.
scripts.hook: Buying an existing franchise location and opening a new one are two different financing conversations.
scripts.script: Buying an existing franchise location and opening a new one are two different financing conversations. A new unit has no track record, so the numbers are projections. A resale comes with an operating history you can review. A resale is also a transfer. Item seventeen of the franchise disclosure document summarizes the transfer terms, and Item six may list a transfer fee. And it's a change of ownership. As of October twenty twenty-six, under the SBA's updated rules, a seven-A change of ownership generally needs an independent business valuation, ordered by the lender. Confirm it with your lender. For either path, if you want SBA financing, the brand has to be on the SBA Franchise Directory. Check the current list. Which fits you depends on your cash, your goals and your comfort with uncertainty. Weighing a resale against a new unit? Send us a DM.
scripts.cta: Weighing a resale against a new unit? Send us a DM.
scripts.recording_notes_es: Plano medio. Usa las manos para separar las dos opciones: izquierda para la unidad nueva, derecha para la reventa, y mantén ese mismo lado durante todo el video. Ritmo pausado en la parte de la valuación. Tono neutro, sin favorecer ninguna opción. Mirada directa en el CTA.
scripts.adaptation_note_es: Original. Usa el mecanismo genérico de comparación fila por fila, sin tomar nada de otros creadores.

fact_refs.claim: FDD Item 17 summarizes renewal, termination, transfer and dispute-resolution terms; Item 6 may list a transfer fee
Under SOP 50 10 8.1 (effective Oct 1, 2026), every change of ownership needs an independent valuation commissioned by the lender (industry source; confirm before airing)
Brands meeting the FTC franchise definition must be on the SBA Franchise Directory for franchisees to get SBA financing; check the current Directory

scripts.why_selected_es: Ningún guion de ayer comparó reventa con unidad nueva. Es una decisión real previa a pedir financiamiento, así que atrae DMs de compradores en etapa activa.
scripts.what_to_measure_es: DMs calificados que mencionen reventa o unidad nueva, compartidos, retención al 50% y visitas al perfil. Las vistas no son leads.
qa_issues: La valuación independiente obligatoria en todo cambio de propiedad bajo la 8.1 tiene solo fuente de la industria (S10). La investigación indica 'reportedly' y 'confirm before airing'. Decirle al espectador 'Confirm it with your lender' no sustituye esa verificación interna. Arreglo: confirmarlo en el texto oficial de la SOP 50 10 8.1 antes de grabar o quitar la frase.

'For either path, if you want SBA financing, the brand has to be on the SBA Franchise Directory' omite la condición. Arreglo: 'if the brand meets the Federal Trade Commission's franchise definition, it has to be on the SBA Franchise Directory', como ya se hace en R10.

scripts.topic: [Buying a franchise] Checklist: use FDD Item 20 to call current and former franchisees, with 4 cash-flow questions
scripts.audience: Prospective franchisees in due diligence who have received an FDD
scripts.problem: Buyers rely on the franchisor's pitch and skip talking to franchisees, so their assumptions stay unchecked.
scripts.amount_context: No amounts used.
scripts.hook: The most useful part of a franchise disclosure document might be a list of names.
scripts.script: The most useful part of a franchise disclosure document might be a list of names. It's called Item twenty. Along with outlet data, it lists current franchisees and franchisees who recently left the system. The Federal Trade Commission's franchise guide encourages talking with both. Here are four questions worth asking. One: how long did it take before the business covered its own costs? Two: what do you actually pay in ongoing fees each month? Three: what costs surprised you in the first year? Four: how much working capital, the cash to cover day-to-day costs, did you really need to get through the start? Write down their answers, and talk to more than one person, including someone who left. Save this before your first call.
scripts.cta: Save this before your first call.
scripts.recording_notes_es: Plano medio, tono de consejo práctico. Levanta los dedos uno a uno en cada pregunta (1 a 4) y deja una pausa corta entre una y otra. Mira a cámara al leer cada pregunta, como si se la estuviera haciendo a un franquiciado. Énfasis suave en 'including someone who left'.
scripts.adaptation_note_es: Original. Usa el mecanismo genérico de checklist numerado.

fact_refs.claim: FDD Item 20 gives outlet data and lists current franchisees and franchisees who recently left the system
The FTC's Consumer Guide encourages talking with current and former franchisees (paraphrased, no quotation)

scripts.why_selected_es: Es otro ítem del FDD (Item 20) y otra fuente: otros franquiciados, no el comprador. Es muy guardable como lista antes de las llamadas.
scripts.what_to_measure_es: Guardados, compartidos, retención hasta la pregunta 4 y DMs de compradores en due diligence. Las vistas no son leads.

scripts.topic: [Buying a franchise] Direct statement: a multi-unit deal is a schedule you promise to keep, and each unit still needs its own funding plan
scripts.audience: Ambitious prospective franchisees considering multi-unit or area development agreements
scripts.problem: Buyers sign development schedules with deadlines and fees before they've worked out how later units would be funded.
scripts.amount_context: No amounts used.
scripts.hook: Signing for three franchise units doesn't mean you have funding for three units.
scripts.script: Signing for three franchise units doesn't mean you have funding for three units. A multi-unit deal is a schedule you promise to keep. In a development agreement, you commit to opening units by certain deadlines. Development fees show up in Items five and six of the franchise disclosure document, and territory rights in Item twelve. Now the part that's easy to overlook. Depending on the agreement, missing a deadline may mean losing your exclusive territory, or even the development agreement itself. So unit one might open on time. But units two and three each need their own funding, on their own timeline, and none of that comes with the signature. Before you sign, map out how each unit on the schedule would be funded. Share this with anyone you're going in with.
scripts.cta: Share this with anyone you're going in with.
scripts.recording_notes_es: Abre con una afirmación firme y mirada fija, sin sonreír los primeros dos segundos. Cuenta las unidades con los dedos (uno, dos, tres). Baja la voz en 'Now the part that's easy to overlook'. Cierre calmado y de consejo, sin dramatizar.
scripts.adaptation_note_es: Original. No se emula V16, que es un ejemplo negativo con promesas de ganancias. Se usa el mecanismo genérico de afirmación contraintuitiva seguida de explicación.

fact_refs.claim: Development fees are disclosed in FDD Items 5 and 6 and territory rights in Item 12; the development schedule is set in the development agreement
Depending on the agreement, missing development deadlines may mean losing territorial exclusivity or the development agreement itself

scripts.why_selected_es: Nadie cubrió multi-unidad ayer. La frase contraintuitiva del gancho favorece el descubrimiento y que se comparta entre socios.
scripts.what_to_measure_es: Compartidos, retención en los primeros 3 segundos, nuevos seguidores y visitas al perfil, y DMs sobre acuerdos de desarrollo. Las vistas no son leads.
qa_issues: No bloqueante: 'units two and three each need their own funding, on their own timeline' suena absoluto, porque algunas estructuras financian varias unidades juntas. Sugerencia: 'units two and three still have to be funded, on the schedule's timeline, and none of that comes with the signature'.

scripts.topic: [Buying a franchise] Question: What is a conversion franchise, and what changes when an existing owner joins a brand?
scripts.audience: Current independent owners (service, home services, restaurants) considering joining a franchise system
scripts.problem: Existing owners don't know about the conversion option or what joining a franchise means for disclosures, fees and SBA eligibility.
scripts.amount_context: No amounts used.

scripts.topic: [Pillar: Buying an existing business] SDE vs. EBITDA in plain English: two ways to measure a business's earnings, who uses which, and why listings show both
scripts.audience: First-time acquisition buyers reading business-for-sale listings and broker packages
scripts.problem: Buyers compare listings that measure earnings differently and overestimate what is left to pay a loan and a manager.
scripts.amount_context: No dollar amounts used. The provisional ~USD 300,000 figure is not mentioned.
scripts.hook: Two business listings both say "earnings." But one means SDE and the other means EBITDA, and those are not the same number.
scripts.script: Two business listings both say "earnings." But one means SDE and the other means EBITDA, and those are not the same number. SDE stands for seller's discretionary earnings. It's generally pre-tax earnings before interest, depreciation and amortization, plus one owner's full compensation and certain one-time or discretionary expenses. EBITDA means earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization. In valuation, it usually keeps a market-rate manager's salary as an expense. So here's the key difference: the owner's paycheck. In SDE, it's added back. In EBITDA, it stays as a cost. In practice, SDE is commonly used for smaller, owner-run businesses, and EBITDA for larger ones with professional management. Either way, lenders generally check earnings against tax returns, and add-backs usually need documentation. These are general definitions, not valuation advice. Save this for the next listing you read.
scripts.cta: Save this for the next listing you read.
scripts.recording_notes_es: Plano medio, mirando a cámara, energía tranquila y didáctica. Al decir 'SDE' y 'EBITDA' usar las manos como dos columnas (izquierda y derecha). En 'the owner's paycheck' hacer una pausa breve y mover la mano de una columna a la otra. Ritmo pausado en las definiciones; no leer de forma acelerada. Sonrisa leve en el CTA final.
scripts.adaptation_note_es: Guion original. No se basa en ningún creador de referencia; el mecanismo es una comparación lado a lado con un único elemento (el sueldo del dueño) como momento de revelación.

fact_refs.claim: SDE is generally pre-tax earnings before interest, depreciation and amortization, plus one owner's total compensation and discretionary or one-time items.
EBITDA is earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization; in valuation it usually keeps a market-rate manager's salary as an expense.
SDE is commonly used for smaller owner-run businesses and EBITDA for larger businesses with professional management (no dollar cutoff given).
Lenders generally check earnings against tax returns, and add-backs usually need documentation.

scripts.why_selected_es: Llena un vacío de vocabulario: los guiones de ayer (DSCR, precio vs. número del lender) daban por sentado qué significa 'earnings'. Es un concepto que confunde a compradores primerizos y tiene alto valor de guardado como referencia.
scripts.what_to_measure_es: Guardados (objetivo principal), retención hasta el momento de 'the owner's paycheck', compartidos y visitas al perfil. Las vistas no son leads; observar si llegan DMs con preguntas sobre listings concretos.
qa_issues: Sin problemas. Incluye la aclaración 'not valuation advice' y no da un corte en dólares.

scripts.topic: [Pillar: Buying an existing business] Due diligence basics: a 5-area checklist of what a buyer verifies about the target business before closing
scripts.audience: Acquisition buyers with an LOI or offer in progress
scripts.problem: Buyers treat diligence as a formality and find issues late in the process, which can affect both the deal and the loan.
scripts.amount_context: No dollar amounts used. The provisional ~USD 300,000 figure is not mentioned.
scripts.hook: Your offer got accepted. Now comes the part that's meant to protect you: due diligence.
scripts.script: Your offer got accepted. Now comes the part that's meant to protect you: due diligence. That's the verification work before closing. Here are five common areas to check. One: financials. Do the seller's statements match the tax returns? In SBA acquisitions, lenders generally verify the seller's numbers against IRS tax transcripts. Two: cash flow. Does the money actually come in the way the listing says? Three: the lease. Under SBA rules, as of October twenty twenty-six and subject to change, the lease term, including renewal options the business alone can use, generally needs to be at least as long as the loan term. Confirm the current version with your lender. Four: key contracts. What carries over, and what ends with the seller? Five: inventory, plus zoning and environmental matters. Bring in an attorney and a CPA for this. Save this before your next offer.
scripts.cta: Save this before your next offer.
scripts.recording_notes_es: Plano medio, mirando a cámara. Tono sereno, de acompañamiento, no de alarma. Marcar cada punto con los dedos (uno a cinco) y hacer una micro-pausa entre puntos. Common diligence areas include contracts, leases, cash flow, inventory, and zoning and environmental matters.

scripts.topic: [Pillar: Buying an existing business] Hypothetical scenario: two partners, one wants out. A partner buyout can be financed as a partial change of ownership
scripts.audience: Current co-owners where one partner wants to exit; existing owners looking for funding
scripts.problem: Owners don't realize a partner buyout can be a financed change of ownership with its own valuation and equity considerations, so they improvise funding or delay the exit.
scripts.amount_context: No dollar amounts used. Hypothetical fifty-fifty ownership split only. The provisional ~USD 300,000 figure is not mentioned.
scripts.hook: Your business partner wants out. Buying their share? That's an acquisition too.
scripts.script: Your business partner wants out. Buying their share? That's an acquisition too. Here's a hypothetical. Two partners own a business fifty-fifty. One wants to retire. The other wants to stay and buy that half. Instead of draining the company's cash, the staying partner looks at financing. As of October twenty twenty-six, the SBA lists complete or partial changes of ownership as eligible uses of seven-A loans. That's an SBA-guaranteed loan made by a lender. Rules can change, and every deal still needs lender approval. But here's the first big question, and it's not the rate. What is the business actually worth? Under the current SBA rules, every change of ownership reportedly needs an independent business valuation. And equity requirements in a partial buyout can differ from a full purchase. Your attorney handles the partnership agreement side. Facing a partner buyout in the next year? Send us a DM.

scripts.topic: [Pillar: Buying an existing business] Question: what happens to the seller's existing liabilities and the lease when you buy a business (asset vs. stock purchase; lease term)
scripts.audience: First-time acquisition buyers early in deal evaluation
scripts.problem: Buyers don't understand how existing liabilities and the premises lease carry over; a short lease can derail financing late in the process.
scripts.amount_context: No dollar amounts used. The provisional ~USD 300,000 figure is not mentioned.
scripts.hook: The seller still owes money on the business. Does that become your problem?
scripts.script: The seller still owes money on the business. Does that become your problem? It depends on the deal structure. In an asset purchase, you buy the business's assets, not the legal company. Generally, you don't take on the seller's liabilities. In a stock purchase, you buy the company, and generally its liabilities come with it. Exceptions exist, so talk to your attorney and CPA. Now the part that's easy to check too late: the lease. Under SBA rules, as of October twenty twenty-six and subject to change, the lease term, including renewal options only the business can exercise, generally needs to run at least as long as the loan term. Confirm the current version with your lender. Read the lease early. How much time is left, and how does it transfer to you? Questions about an acquisition? Send us a DM.
scripts.cta: Questions about an acquisition? Send us a DM.
scripts.recording_notes_es: Plano medio, empezar con expresión de pregunta genuina mirando a cámara. Separar claramente las dos respuestas (asset vs. stock) con un gesto de mano a cada lado. Antes de 'the lease' hacer una pausa breve e inclinarse ligeramente hacia la cámara. Tono calmado, sin dramatizar.

scripts.topic: [Pillar: Buying an existing business] Myth vs. reality: 'An earn-out is basically the same as a seller note.' What an earn-out is and how it's reportedly treated in SBA 7(a) acquisitions
scripts.audience: Acquisition buyers negotiating price gaps with sellers
scripts.problem: Buyers propose earn-outs to bridge valuation gaps without knowing SBA financing may not allow contingent price structures, which can force a late restructure.
scripts.amount_context: No dollar amounts used. The provisional ~USD 300,000 figure is not mentioned.
scripts.hook: "We'll just do an earn-out." In an SBA deal, that may not fly.
scripts.script: "We'll just do an earn-out." In an SBA deal, that may not fly. Here's the myth: an earn-out is basically the same as a seller note. Reality: they're different tools. An earn-out is a future payment to the seller that depends on how the business performs after closing. Hit the targets, the seller gets more. Miss them, the seller gets less. Here's why that matters. As of October twenty twenty-six, industry sources report that seller earn-outs aren't allowed in SBA seven-A acquisitions, because the purchase price can't be contingent. Seven-A is an SBA-guaranteed loan from a lender. A buyer rebate tied to performance after closing is reportedly allowed. These rules can change, so confirm with your lender and attorney before putting an earn-out in an offer. Know someone negotiating a business purchase? Send them this.
scripts.cta: Know someone negotiating a business purchase? Send them this.

scripts.topic: [Getting loan ready] How to build a use-of-funds statement line by line, with each line tied to a document and both sides adding up
scripts.audience: Any borrower preparing a request (franchise, acquisition, growth or working capital)
scripts.problem: Borrowers submit a single lump-sum request with no itemized, documented breakdown.
scripts.amount_context: Hypothetical total project uses of $250,000 ($120,000 equipment, $80,000 build-out, $40,000 working capital, $10,000 closing costs and fees). Illustrative only; this is not the provisional ~$300,000 figure.
scripts.hook: "I need about this much" isn't a use of funds.
scripts.script: "I need about this much" isn't a use of funds. Here's what one looks like, line by line. This is a hypothetical. Line one: equipment, one hundred twenty thousand dollars, backed by a vendor quote. Line two: build-out, eighty thousand, backed by a contractor bid. Line three: working capital, the cash to cover day-to-day costs, forty thousand, backed by your monthly expense budget. Line four: closing costs and fees, ten thousand, backed by written estimates. Total uses: two hundred fifty thousand. Then the other side: your loan request plus your own cash has to add up to that same number. If the two columns don't match, something's missing. And remember, SBA loan proceeds must go to eligible uses. As of October twenty twenty-six, seven-A uses include working capital, equipment, real estate and changes of ownership. Save this for when you build yours.
scripts.cta: Save this for when you build yours.
scripts.recording_notes_es: Plano medio, tono de taller práctico. Señala hacia un lado en cada línea, como si escribiera en una pizarra imaginaria. Pausa después de 'Total uses'. En 'Then the other side', gesto de balanza con ambas manos. Ritmo constante y sin apuro.
scripts.adaptation_note_es: Original. Usa el mecanismo genérico de tabla que se completa paso a paso.

As of Oct 2026, 7(a) uses include working capital, equipment, real estate and changes of ownership
All line items, the $250,000 total and the matching of loan plus own cash to total uses are a hypothetical arithmetic illustration

La suma (ciento veinte, ochenta, cuarenta y diez mil, total doscientos cincuenta mil) es correcta y está etiquetada como hipotética.

scripts.topic: [Getting loan ready] Question: What are interim financials and a business debt schedule?
scripts.audience: Existing owners seeking growth or working-capital funding, and acquisition teams preparing packages
scripts.problem: Owners hand over only tax returns and lack current-year statements and a clear list of business debts.
scripts.amount_context: Hypothetical debt-schedule row: equipment loan with $40,000 remaining and $1,000 a month, paid off in 2029. Illustrative only.
scripts.hook: Your tax return shows last year. So what shows this year?
scripts.script: Your tax return shows last year. So what shows this year? That's where interim financials come in. Interim financial statements are your current year-to-date statements, usually a profit and loss statement and a balance sheet. Profit and loss shows what came in and what went out. The balance sheet shows what the business owns and owes right now. Then there's the second document: a debt schedule. It's simply a list of every business debt you have. The SBA's seven-A borrower information form, Form nineteen-nineteen, collects information on existing debt, so it helps to have this ready. Here's a hypothetical row: equipment loan, forty thousand dollars remaining, one thousand a month, paid off in twenty twenty-nine, plus the lender's name. One row per debt. Two documents, one purpose: showing where the business stands today. Which one do you already have ready? Reply and tell us.
scripts.cta: Which one do you already have ready? Reply and tell us.

scripts.topic: [Getting loan ready] Objection: 'It's a business loan, so why are my personal finances involved?' Personal guaranty, Form 413 and the credit elsewhere test
scripts.audience: First-time borrowers (franchise and acquisition buyers) surprised by personal disclosure requests
scripts.problem: Borrowers resist or delay personal disclosures because they don't understand why an SBA business loan involves the owner's own finances.
scripts.amount_context: No dollar amounts used (only the 20% ownership threshold, a program rule).
scripts.hook: "The business is borrowing, not me."
scripts.script: "The business is borrowing, not me." Fair point. But with an SBA loan, your personal finances are part of the picture. Here's why, in three parts. One: the personal guaranty. As of October twenty twenty-six, owners of twenty percent or more generally must give a full personal guaranty. That means you personally back the loan. Two: the personal financial statement. That's SBA Form four-thirteen. It's completed by owners of twenty percent or more, by any guarantor, and by certain others like proprietors and general partners. Three: the credit elsewhere test. Lenders must check that the business and its owners of twenty percent or more don't have readily available funds that make the SBA loan unnecessary. There are reasonable exceptions. It's built into the program. Confirm the details with your lender. Share this with anyone buying a business with you.
scripts.cta: Share this with anyone buying a business with you.
scripts.recording_notes_es: Abre diciendo la objeción con tono de cliente algo molesto y luego asiente con calma en 'Fair point'. Cuenta 'One, Two, Three' con los dedos. Tono sereno y explicativo, nunca de regaño. Mirada directa en el cierre.
scripts.adaptation_note_es: Original. Usa el mecanismo genérico de objeción seguida de tres razones.

fact_refs.claim: Owners of 20% or more generally must give a full personal guaranty
SBA Form 413 is completed by each proprietor, general partner, LLC managing member, owner of 20% or more, and any guarantor

Under SOP 50 10 8, lenders must check that the applicant and owners of 20% or more don't have readily available funds that make the SBA loan unnecessary (credit elsewhere), with reasonable exceptions; not a return of the old Personal Resources Test

scripts.why_selected_es: Responde una resistencia frecuente del comprador primerizo con tres reglas concretas. Es fácil de compartir entre socios y ayuda al descubrimiento.

scripts.topic: [Getting loan ready] Storytime-style hypothetical: two would-be borrowers in a first lender conversation, one with a one-page summary and one with only an idea
scripts.audience: Buyers and owners planning to approach a lender in the next six to twelve months
scripts.problem: People go into a first lender conversation unprepared and leave without useful feedback, even though the first call is often a screening conversation where basic numbers are expected.
scripts.amount_context: No dollar amounts used. Only the 'six to twelve months' planning window. The ~USD 300,000 figure is not referenced.
scripts.hook: Two people have their first lender call. Only one gets real answers.
scripts.script: Two people have their first lender call. Only one gets real answers. This is a hypothetical. Person A shows up with an idea: "I want to buy a business. How much can I get?" Person B brings a one-page summary: what they're buying, how much they need, the use of funds, how much of their own cash is available, and their timeline to purchase. In this story, the first question both get is the same: "What's the money for?" Person A has to guess. Person B answers in one sentence, and the call moves on to real feedback: what's missing, and what to prepare next. That doesn't mean Person B gets approved. It means the call was actually useful. Planning to buy or fund a business in the next six to twelve months and want to prepare for that first conversation? Send us a DM.
scripts.cta: Planning to buy or fund a business in the next six to twelve months and want to prepare for that first conversation? Send us a DM.
scripts.recording_notes_es: Tono de contar una historia, cercano. Para Person A, girar levemente la cabeza a un lado; para Person B, al otro, así se distinguen sin cambiar la voz. Pausa de suspenso antes de 'What's the money for?'. Decir 'That doesn't mean Person B gets approved' con calma y en serio. En la invitación final, mirada directa y ritmo pausado.
scripts.adaptation_note_es: Guion original; no adapta ninguna referencia externa. Mecanismo propio: una historia hipotética con contraste A/B y un bucle abierto ('la primera pregunta que les hacen a los dos'). No es la historia de ningún creador ni una experiencia de Kevin.

fact_refs.claim: Both characters and the whole conversation are hypothetical; preparing a one-page summary (what, how much, use of funds, own cash, timeline) is presented as general preparation guidance, with no implication of approval
General loan-preparation guidance context (Lender Match is not mentioned in the spoken text)

scripts.why_selected_es: Es el guion de conversión del lote. La invitación filtra por intención y plazo (seis a doce meses), lo que atrae mensajes de gente con un plan real. El formato de historia A/B suma variedad y no repite R20 de ayer (cómo elegir prestamista).
scripts.what_to_measure_es: Mensajes directos calificados, es decir, que mencionan un plan y un plazo concretos (objetivo principal), además de visitas al perfil y retención hasta el bucle 'What's the money for?'. Las vistas no son leads.
qa_issues: No es grave: el CTA es largo, unas 25 palabras. Se puede acortar a 'Planning to buy or fund a business in the next six to twelve months? Send us a DM.' Toda la historia está marcada como hipotética.
